programme.title: Road absurdities
programme.desc: We will see an expressway with a speed limit of 50 km/h and a micro-roundabout in Kielce.In Rzeszów, attention is drawn to the accumulation of mirrors on the main road, and in Warsaw - another intersection with a road to nowhere, although with full infrastructure.In Pawłowice there is a frame for sound-absorbing screens separating the track from the road.We will see an example of improper use of U12c bollards in Lublin, a strange roadside sign on a road without a shoulder in Łuków, and another local road in Łuków which, in addition to holes, also has a speed bump.We will also look at sharp energy-consuming barriers in Święcice, a left turn leading straight to the barrier on DK74 and a road in Wrocław that officials closed instead of repairing.

programme.title: Road absurdities
programme.desc: Kamil Jaśkowski and Krzysiek Ruszała will check where the roundabout with only two access roads in Bielsko-Biała comes from.In Bieruń we will see a power pole on the road, in Tychy - an innovative bus lane, and in Gliwice - a closed street full of signs and barriers.In Warsaw's Ursynów we will find a dangerous bicycle path, in Natolin - a new roundabout that is of no use to anyone, and in Tuchola we will focus on signs obscured by roadside trees.Słupsk will surprise us with a railway crossing in the street, and Gwizd - with fancy private barriers on the access roads to the property.In Tomaszów Mazowiecki, the crew of the S201 siren will admire the abundance of signs informing about the main road and the simultaneous lack of yield signs on minor roads, and in Łódź - a sidewalk with 11 manholes within an 8-meter radius.
